In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our analysis shows that the learning of one-hidden-layer neural network is more challenging when the input data is more concentrated around a few means, or when there is a large variance among the input data.

, for one-hidden-layer neural network with sigmoid activation, the sample complexity of learning the model from Gaussian mixture model data is determined by the number of Gaussian components, and by the variances and the means of these components.

, for the considered learning setup and algorithm, the sample complexity and the convergence rate are both increasing functions of the parameters of Gaussian mixtures, which are the means and variances of the Gaussian distributions in the mixture model.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the sample complexity and convergence rate depend on the input distributions.
the learning problem of neural networks is more challenging for Gaussian mixture models with a large mean, or small variance in each Gaussian distribution.

the learning problem is more challenging when the input data is concentrated around a single Gaussian distribution, and it is more robust when the input data has a mixture of Gaussian distributions with various means and variances.
